newsitem.title: DUBAI: Al Jouf Agri to build Saudi's second sugar refiner.
newsitem.headline: Al Jouf Agri to build Saudi's second sugar refiner.

text.p: A Saudi Arabian agricultural company has received government approval to build the kingdom's second sugar refinery to produce 120,000 tonnes of white sugar a year, a Saudi-owned newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The London-based Asharq al-Awsat quoted Prince Sultan bin Abdul-Rahman Sudeiri, prince of the Jouf region and chairman of the Al-Jouf Agricultural Development Co, as saying the company received approval from the industry ministry to build the plant.
He said the refinery in Jouf in northern Saudi Arabia will produce 120,000 tonnes of white sugar and 42,000 tonnes of molasses.
He said the project's capital was 335 million riyals, 50 percent of which would be financed by the Saudi Industrial Development Fund (SIDF).
He did not say when construction or commercial production at the refinery will start.
The plant planned by Al-Jouf Agricultural, which is involved in agriculture and animal feed production, will be the second sugar refinery in the kingdom.

Saudi Arabia's United Sugar Co (USC) started commissioning its 500,000 tonne refinery in February. The start of production there means that imports of white sugar by the kingdom will drop sharply and the country will become a predominantly raw sugar market.
The USC refinery is 51 percent owned by Savola -- Saudi Arabia's biggest food group, 15 percent by Britain's Tate and Lyle Plc and the rest by Saudi sugar trading firms.
Per capita consumption of sugar in the Arabian peninsula is among the world's highest at around 30 kg.
